headline: Approved CAVA Group special permit at 96 Tower Road and $320,000 in CPA funds for Gore Place window restoration.
summary: Members approved a special permit for CAVA Group at 96 Tower Road, with 12 in favor and none opposed. They also approved CPA funds of $320,000, $85,000, and $52.768 for restoration projects. The Sweetgreen special permit request for 96 Tower Road was referred to a committee, and its hearing was continued to November 23, 2026.

plain_text:
1
Waltham City Council 
Minutes of the Meeting of 
October 13, 2026
President Logan called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. 
 
Artie Kronenfeld from the Waltham Times was recognized as recording the meeting.
Present: Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Harris, Hanley, King, LaCava, LaFauci, 
LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and President Logan. 
Absent: Katz, Vidal.
City Clerk Vizard recited the Council Prayer followed by President Logan leading all present in the 
Pledge of Allegiance. Councillor Durkee for a moment of silence for all our troops serving all over 
the world and for those supporting them.
President Logan announced that Councillor Katz is in the hospital recovering from surgery,
and asked everyone to keep Councillor Katz and his family in their thoughts and prayers.
Councillor LaFauci spoke on the passing of William “Bill” Creonte, Sr. and asked for a moment of 
silence in his memory.
Councillor LeBlanc moved approval of the regular City Council meeting minutes of September 28, 
2026. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Clerk Vizard read Rule 86.
First Joint Public Hearing: Special Permit application at 96 Tower Road for Sweetgreen Boston, 
LLC
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Michael Connors of 689 Main Street, 
Waltham, MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one 
in opposition and no one in a neutral position to the ordinance President Logan closed that part 
of the public hearing and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillors 
LaFauci and Bradley-MacArthur asked questions on the matter. Attorney Connors provided 
answers. With no further questions President Logan closed the public hearing and referred the 
matter to the Ordinances and Rules Committee. President Logan recessed the public hearing to 
date certain of Monday, November 23, 2026 at 7:30 p.m.
Second Public Hearing: Special Permit application at 96 Tower Road for CAVA Group 
(Recessed from 8/3/26)
Councillor Harris made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to waive the reading of the 
public hearing notice. Councillor Harris made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to 
suspend Rule 8 to take the report of the Ordinances and Rules Committee regarding the Special 
Permit application for CAVA Group out of order. Councillor Harris moved to approve the 
application. Roll call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, King, LaCava, 
LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin and Tzioumis.
Opposed: None.
Absent: Katz, Vidal.
Presiding: Logan.
2
Approved: 12-0-2-1.
Communications from the Mayor
1. The Mayor respectfully requested confirmation of the appointment of Richard Pizzi, Jr. as 
a permanent member of the Waltham Council on Aging to fill a vacancy. Referred to the 
Committee of the Whole.
2. The Mayor respectfully requested the confirmation of the appointment of Marcia 
MacClary as a permanent member of the Waltham Council on Aging to fill a vacancy. 
Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
3. The Mayor respectfully requested an appropriation in the amount of $120,000 from the 
Cemetery Sale of Lots & Graves account to purchase a new Chevrolet Silverado 3500 
truck with snowplow package for the use of the Cemetery Division. Referred to the 
Finance Committee.
4. The Mayor respectfully requested the adoption of an Amendment to the Compensation 
Ordinance pertaining to personnel costs associated with elections. Councillor Harris 
moved to suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without Committee reference for the 
purpose of giving the matter a first reading. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Councillor Harris made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to give the 
Compensation Ordinance amendment a first reading. Referred to the Ordinances and 
Rules Committee.
5. The Mayor respectfully requested approval of a loan authorization in the amount of 
$462,755 for additional design services for the inclusion of the Fire Administration Wing 
of the Police Station. Referred to the Long Term Debt & Capital Planning Committee.
6. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of EECBG additional grant funds in the 
amount of $9,000 from the Department of Energy for the installation of new EV Chargers 
in the City’s public parking lots project. Referred to the Finance Committee.
7. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of a grant in the amount of $52,152 from the
Office of Grants and Research (OGR) to support the FFY2027 Municipal Road safety 
(MRS) Program. Referred to the Finance Committee.
8. The Mayor respectfully requested an opportunity for a presentation of the plan for the 
Police Station and Fire and 911 Headquarters by Tecton Architects for Monday, October 
19, 2026. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
9. The Mayor respectfully requested your advisement on the easement and parking spaces at 
210-220 Moody Street. This is related to the Special Permit application at 210 Moody 
Street. Referred to the Ordinances and Rules Committee.
Applications and Licenses
All Applications and Licenses referred to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
1. Fortune Tellers license renewal – 24 Crescent Street STE 401F– Minwoo Park
2. Extended Hours renewal – 12 Harvard Street – CVS Pharmacy #114
3
Committee Reports
Committee of the Whole
1. The Committee of the Whole recommended the communication from Attorney Connors 
regarding Hobbs Brook be filed. Councillor LeBlanc moved that the action of the 
Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and 
the matter was filed.
2. The Committee of the Whole recommended the acceptance of additional lists of building 
names or parcels at 190 Trapelo Road within Parcel 2A-2, parcel 2B, Parcel 3A &3B be 
filed. Councillor LeBlanc moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the 
Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was filed.
3. The Committee of the Whole recommended the Eversource Resolution be filed. 
Councillor LeBlanc moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. 
The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was filed.
4. The Committee of the Whole recommended the acceptance of a draft for Cardinal Cottage 
affordable housing application package be filed. Councillor LeBlanc moved that the action
of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, 
and the matter was filed.
Ordinances and Rules
1. The Ordinances and Rules Committee recommended the Special Permit application for 
CAVA Group, Inc. at 96 Tower Road be approved. This matter was handled earlier in the 
evening.
Long Term Debt & Capital Planning
1. The Long Term Debt & Capital Planning Committee recommended the CPC 
recommendation for an allocation of $320,000 of CPA funds for Window Restoration at 
Gore Place be approved. Councillor Durkee moved that the action of the Committee be the
action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was 
approved.
2. The Long Term Debt & Capital Planning Committee recommended the CPC 
recommendation for an allocation of $85,000 of CPA funds for Exterior Restoration of 
Community Day Center 20 Felton Street Location be approved. Councillor Durkee 
moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was 
approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved.
3. The Long Term Debt & Capital Planning Committee recommended the CPC 
recommendation for an allocation of $52.768 of additional CPA funds for Steeple 
Preservation and Restoration at First Parish Church be approved. Councillor Bradley-
MacArthur recused herself. Councillor Durkee moved that the action of the Committee be
the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was 
approved.
Licenses and Franchises
1. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Fuel Storage license at 245 
Fifth Avenue for ALP PHOP Manager, LLC & NWALP PHOP owner be approved.
4
Councillor Brasco moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. 
The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved.
2. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Rule 95 Utility Master Plan 
Resolution be approved. Councillor Brasco moved that the action of the Committee be 
the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was 
approved.
3. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Fuel Storage licenses at 40 -  
50 & 60 Sylvan Road for ARE-MA be approved. Councillor Brasco moved that the 
action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a 
voice vote, and the matter was approved.
Unfinished Business & Other Business
Tabled Items
 66 Brewster Road (Tabled 6/9/25)
Rule 58
 Communication from FD Special Opportunities II_A, LLC
Recessed Public Hearings
 Special Permit MICOL at 220 Moody Street recessed on 8/3/26 (10/26/26)
 Special Permit CAVA Group Inc. at 96 Tower Road recessed 8/3/26 (10/13/26)
 Special Permit Modification Dyer’s Crescent Suites, LLC 287 Crescent Street recessed 
9/14/26 (11/23/26)
 Special Permit Service Credit Union 995 Main Street recessed 9/14/26 (11/23/26)
With no further matters Councillor Harris made a motion to adjourn. The motion was approved 
by a voice vote. President Logan declared the meeting adjourned at 7:58 p.m.
Respectfully submitted by:
Cathy Magliarditi
Executive Assistant to the City Clerk
October 19, 2026
